title: Risk, Resilience and Recidivism: Do Protective Factors Measured by the SAPROF-SO Improve Prediction of Sexual Reoffending With an Australian Sample?
abstract: The current study contributes to research evaluating the Structured Assessment of PROtective Factors against Sexual Offending (SAPROF-SO). A sample of incarcerated Australian males with sexual offending histories ( N = 138) were retrospectively scored on the SAPROF-SO and followed up for an average of 5.5 years post-release. Official reconviction data were used to examine predictive validity. Participants’ Static-99R and STABLE-2007 scores were also collected to assess the incremental predictive validity of the SAPROF-SO. SAPROF-SO Total scores did not significantly predict absence of sexual reoffending. However, the Adaptive Sexuality subscale significantly predicted no further sexual offence convictions (area under the curve = .73, p = .002). Cox proportional hazards regression indicated the Adaptive Sexuality subscale provided significant incremental predictive validity beyond the Static-99R and conceptually similar STABLE-2007 items. Implications for assessment and treatment are discussed.
